PullRequest.Title: Make the Integrated Browser an external URI opener
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #342934

Part of #342050. Stacked on #342897 (merge that first; this PR's base is its branch).

The Integrated Browser's localhost link opener was a second `IExternalOpener` next to `ExternalUriOpenerService`, with its own URL checks. It registers first, so it took localhost links before the `workbench.externalUriOpeners` setting or an explicitly requested opener were considered, and it never appeared in the "How would you like to open" prompt or in Quick Open's link handlers.

## Changes

- The Integrated Browser is now an opener of `ExternalUriOpenerService` (`workbench.integratedBrowser`, "Open in Integrated Browser"): `Preferred` for localhost and all-interfaces links when `workbench.browser.openLocalhostLinks` is enabled, `Option` for any other web link. So Quick Open lists it for every web link, and it is the default for localhost links when the setting is on.
- Optional openers no longer cause the "choose an opener" prompt next to a single opener of `Default` priority, so offering the Integrated Browser everywhere does not add prompts.
- `IExternalUriOpener.openExternalUri` receives the link as written (`href`) instead of a re-parsed URI, so the Integrated Browser keeps the link's encoding (e.g. `%26` in a query), as it did when it got the string directly. Extension openers still receive a URI over the API.
- Web link schemes match case-insensitively (`HTTP://localhost:3000`), and "Preview in Editor" builds the source URI of a forwarded port with its tunnel's protocol (the Integrated Browser navigates to it when using the remote proxy).

Behavior differences: configured and requested openers now win over the Integrated Browser for localhost links; an unknown requested opener id falls back to the normal selection.

## Screenshots

Quick Open with this PR on top of #342897. With `workbench.browser.openLocalhostLinks` enabled, the Integrated Browser is the default for a localhost link:

![Quick Open for a localhost link listing "Open in Integrated Browser" (Default), "Open in Simple Browser" and "Open in Default Browser"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b68b6c2-f37d-40b7-9426-29e8996df9bc)

For other web links it is offered as an option:

![Quick Open for a PR link listing "Open GitHub Issue or Pull Request" (Default), "Open in Integrated Browser" and "Open in Default Browser"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b22fe65-c86f-4e8a-89e3-7bc850d2d2b8)
## How to test

1. Enable `workbench.browser.openLocalhostLinks`, run **Open URL** with `http://localhost:3999/check?x=a%26b`: it opens in the Integrated Browser with the URL unchanged.
2. Add `"workbench.externalUriOpeners": { "localhost:3999": "default" }` and repeat: it opens in the system browser.
3. Ctrl+P and paste a web link: "Open in Integrated Browser" is listed.

Validation:

- `scripts\test.bat --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/remote/test/browser/remoteExplorer.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/browserView/test/electron-browser/features/localhostLinkOpener.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/externalUriOpener/test/common/externalUriOpenerService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/extHostUriOpener.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/search/test/browser/anythingQuickAccess.test.ts`: passed (63 tests)
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run eslint -- <changed .ts files>`: passed
- Manually in Code OSS: steps 1-3 above: worked

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed registration and full call path are directly traced. Only the exact duration varies by extension state and installed openers.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Extension scanning/activation work and extension-host IPC calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cold latency scales with extension discovery/activation; every warm click issues one concurrent canOpen IPC per registered extension opener for the scheme.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased latency on localhost link opens
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The BlockStartup contribution registered directly with IOpenerService. Its localhost check handled enabled local links, and OpenerService short-circuited without entering extension-backed opener discovery.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Enabled localhost links now await aggregate opener discovery, extension activation, and canOpen checks before the built-in Preferred opener is selected.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: At RIGHT line 617 the contribution stops registering as a direct IExternalOpener and instead joins ExternalUriOpenerService's provider list, whose selection always awaits every provider.
Findings.Title: Keep localhost opens off extension discovery
Findings.Impact: With workbench.browser.openLocalhostLinks enabled, opening a localhost URL can be delayed by cold extension scanning/activation and, thereafter, by extension-host round trips before the Integrated Browser editor appears.
Findings.Evidence: ExternalUriOpenerService.getAllOpenersForUri awaits all providers. MainThreadUriOpeners.getOpeners awaits activateByEvent(onOpenExternalUri:http[s]), then getValidOpeners calls canOpen for every extension opener through proxy.$canOpenUri. Native and web extension initialization starts only at LifecyclePhase.Ready, while this contribution is registered at BlockStartup, so an early open can wait for scanning; warm opens still repeat one canOpen IPC per matching extension opener.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep a fast path for the static Preferred localhost opener: inspect requested/configured overrides first, then avoid activating extension-backed providers when no override applies. Retain full enumeration for explicit extension overrides, prompts, and link-handler listing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an enabled localhost or all-interfaces link in the Integrated Browser
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve/forward the URI, discover all external URI openers, await extension activation and all canOpen results, select the built-in Preferred opener, then create the browser editor and navigate. The newly added extension work is on the critical path before the editor appears.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate extensions for onOpenExternalUri:http[s] across extension hosts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One activation request per extension-host manager on the cold event; manager-level results are cached afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The direct BlockStartup localhost opener handled the link first, so this extension-backed provider was not reached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold activation/scanning must complete before opener discovery returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One concurrent RPC per registered extension opener matching the scheme on every open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No extension opener canOpen RPC was needed after the direct localhost opener returned true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Selection awaits all checks before choosing the Integrated Browser.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/navigate the Integrated Browser editor to the resolved or source localhost URL
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One browser editor/navigation per accepted link.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editor and navigation were created directly by the localhost opener.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after opener selection and determines page-load completion, but its placement and count are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold cost grows with extension discovery/activation and available extension hosts; warm cost grows with the number of registered HTTP(S) extension openers. Effective cardinality is one activation event plus N matching opener checks per click.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Providers are enumerated concurrently with Promise.all; all discovered opener canOpen calls are also launched concurrently. There is no global limiter, and selection waits for the slowest provider/check.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Activation-event promises are cached by ExtensionHostManager after the cold request. There is no cache for per-opener canOpen results, so warm clicks repeat the RPC fan-out. The static Integrated Browser priority is also recomputed per click.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registration, lifecycle order, unconditional provider aggregation, activation await, and RPC fan-out are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension scan duration, remote-host readiness, and the typical number/cost of external URI openers vary by installation. The extra critical-path boundaries are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium boundary-fanout regression: the PR moves the default localhost path behind extension discovery and repeated extension-host checks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type or paste an HTTP(S) link in Quick Open and list link handlers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each accepted valid link query, getLinkHandlers parses the URI, discovers providers, activates relevant extensions, runs canOpen for all openers, and builds picks. Work completes before link-handler picks are shown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold once per scheme/host event, then cached; requested on each valid query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: getLinkHandlers already enumerated MainThreadUriOpeners and awaited this activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can delay the first handler list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One concurrent RPC per registered matching opener for each valid query refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same extension openers were queried before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Handler picks wait for all priorities.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Valid URL query refresh frequency and N registered extension openers; the diff adds only one constant-time in-process opener.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider enumeration and opener checks each use Promise.all. Independent query refreshes are cancellation-driven by Quick Access; activation is cached, while canOpen receives the current token.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Extension activation is cached; opener priorities and handler arrays are not cached. The new Integrated Browser provider contributes one in-process option and one URL/configuration check.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: Quick Open directly calls getLinkHandlers and the provider/check pipeline is explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typing cadence and extension opener count vary, but the expensive boundaries predate the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the diff makes the built-in browser visible but does not add IPC/network cardinality to this already enumerating path.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Look up the tunnel, build the protocol-correct source URI, discover/select an opener for the local URI, then open the selected browser or fall back to the opener service. Discovery precedes navigation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached activation event request and up to one host activation per applicable host on cold use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: OpenPortInPreviewAction already called getOpener before this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One concurrent RPC per registered matching opener.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same getOpener pipeline queried contributed openers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Navigate through the existing forwarded tunnel/local endpoint
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The preview already navigated to tunnel.localUri; only source protocol/string preservation changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines page load after opener selection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected tunnel and N registered URI openers; no loop over all tunnels is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider and canOpen work runs with the same two Promise.all stages as other external URI selection; a single preview action awaits one selection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tunnel state is read from existing forwarded/detected maps. Activation is cached; canOpen results are not. No new cache or negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the action and getOpener call path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tunnel latency and opener count vary, but boundary cardinality is unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: protocol correction and string passing do not increase expensive-boundary count or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup registers the Integrated Browser opener
Scenarios.CriticalPath: During BlockStartup, instantiate LocalhostLinkOpenerContribution and now the delayed ExternalUriOpenerService, register the service with IOpenerService, and add the built-in provider. This synchronous setup precedes workbench rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant one service and one provider per window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous registration only; no asynchronous provider enumeration or browser creation runs at startup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The singleton and provider are retained for the workbench lifetime and disposed through contribution/service ownership. No unbounded keys or per-resource cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor bodies only register linked-list entries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Dependency-proxy construction cost is not measured, but no filesystem/network/IPC/subprocess operation is reached by the constructors.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the PR eagerly instantiates a small service during BlockStartup, but the changed startup path has constant in-process work and no concrete expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files. One medium boundary-fanout regression was submitted for moving default localhost opens behind extension discovery/activation and per-opener IPC. Quick Open, forwarded-port preview, href preservation, opener-choice filtering, and startup registration were traced and did not establish additional diff-introduced performance regressions.
